events.name: node.created
events.description: A node was created through the API. Names the properties supplied, never their values.

events.name: node.renamed
events.description: A node moved to a new key through its alias, such as a repository renamed on its provider (#88). Names the keys it left and took.

events.name: node.merged
events.description: One node was merged into another of its type (#98), by a person through the API or automatically when an artifact's digest was seen. Names both keys, how many edges moved, and who merged it.

events.name: node.merge.skipped
events.description: An automatic merge found when an artifact's digest was seen was not made, because the graph changed under it (#98). Names both keys and the refusal; the write that found it stands.

events.name: node.rejected
events.description: A node write was refused by the ontology. Names the fields at fault, never their values.

events.name: edge.created
events.description: An edge was created through the API.

events.name: graph.store.failed
events.description: A graph store operation failed for a reason other than the domain refusing it, such as Neo4j being unreachable.

events.name: graph.count.failed
events.message: graph count failed; keeping the last counts
events.description: Counting the graph's nodes and edges by type failed, so sdlc_graph_nodes and sdlc_graph_edges keep their last values.

events.name: http.request.rejected
events.description: A request was refused with 400 because its arguments could not be read.

events.name: ingest.deployment.received
events.description: The deploy pipeline reported a deployment, which was applied.

events.name: ingest.seed.received
events.description: The dogfood seed posted a batch, which was applied.

events.name: ingest.unauthorized
events.message: ingest refused without a valid token
events.description: Someone posted to an ingest endpoint without the ingest token.

events.name: principal.registered
events.description: A user registered an identity provider client as a service principal, owned by a team. From now on the client's tokens are let in and its writes are attributed to it.

events.name: principal.deregistered
events.description: A user ended a service principal's registration. The record is kept with a validTo, and the client's tokens are refused from now on.

events.name: principal.refused
events.message: token from an unregistered client refused
events.description: A token the identity provider signed for a client, with no user in it, was refused with 403 because no current service principal registration names the client. Either a client nobody registered, or one since deregistered, is calling the API.

events.name: scope.refused
events.description: A principal the API knows was refused with 403 because its token lacks a graph scope the request needs - graph:read to read, graph:write to change the graph. Names the principal, the method and the scopes, never the path, which can hold a node's key.

events.name: policy.denied
events.description: The authorisation policy refused a request for a reason other than a missing scope - a role, an agent's limits, a type above the caller's clearance, a source the caller may not speak for. Names the principal, its kind, the action and the rule that refused it, never the path, which can hold a node's key.

events.name: policy.redacted
events.description: A read was answered with nodes the caller is not cleared for left out, or with properties above its clearance removed (#30). Names the principal, how many nodes were left out and which properties were removed, never their values.

events.name: policy.loaded
events.description: The API compiled the authorisation policy bundle and will evaluate it in its own process. Names the bundle's revision and where it came from.

events.name: policy.unavailable
events.message: authorisation policy could not be evaluated; refusing the request
events.description: Evaluating the authorisation policy failed, so the request was refused with 503 policy_unavailable rather than answered unchecked. Reads are refused as well as writes, because a read that cannot be filtered could show what the caller may not see.

events.name: auth.anonymous.readonly
events.message: no identity provider; serving reads to anyone and refusing every write
events.description: The API started with no AUTH_ISSUER_URI, the anonymous read-only mode (#118). Reads need no token and every write is refused as read-only, so nothing is written by nobody; AuthGuard lets this start only with SDLC_READ_ONLY=true. Logged on every start.

events.name: ontology.constraints.ensured
events.description: The store has a uniqueness constraint on the key of every node type.

events.name: ontology.version.recorded
events.description: The ontology version this instance runs was written to the graph.

events.name: ontology.migration.baselined
events.message: ontology migration recorded as a baseline
events.description: A shipped migration was recorded as applied without running, because the graph began on its version or a newer one and never held the shape it repairs (#33).

events.name: ontology.migration.applied
events.description: A migration ran in a transaction of its own and was recorded on the graph with its checksum (#33).

events.name: ontology.migration.failed
events.message: ontology migration failed and was rolled back
events.description: A migration failed; its transaction was rolled back, so the graph is as it was before it, and nothing after it ran. At startup the application stops (#33).

events.name: ontology.migrations.pending
events.description: In manual mode the application started with migrations the graph has not had; an admin applies them from the lifecycle page. Health is not affected (#33).

events.name: lifecycle.archive.scheduled
events.description: The archive is enabled and will run on a schedule, in the mode it names (#33).

events.name: lifecycle.archive.finished
events.description: An archive run finished. A dry run changed nothing; export wrote the file; purge wrote the file and then deleted what it wrote (#33).

events.name: lifecycle.archive.failed
events.description: A scheduled archive run could not finish. Nothing is purged that was not first written; the next run retries (#33).

events.name: links.scheduled
events.description: The link engine will resolve every cloud resource on a schedule, as a FULL run of link-engine.

events.name: links.resolution.triggered
events.message: link resolution triggered by a sync run
events.description: A connector's run touched resources or repositories, so a resolution scoped to them was started. Names both runs.

events.name: links.rule.failed
events.message: link rule failed; the resource is left as it was
events.description: A link rule could not read a resource's evidence, so that resource was not resolved in this run, which is partial.

events.name: links.candidate.accepted
events.description: A person accepted a candidate link, which became a manual OWNS_RESOURCE. Names the candidate, both ends and who accepted it.

events.name: links.candidate.rejected
events.description: A person rejected a candidate link; it is not proposed again while its evidence is the same. Names the candidate, both ends and who rejected it.

events.name: links.manual.stated
events.description: A person stated that a repository owns a cloud resource. Names both ends and who stated it.

events.name: links.manual.closed
events.description: A person closed a manual link; the edge keeps its history with validTo set. Names both ends and who closed it.

events.name: connector.scheduled
events.description: A connector will sync on a schedule.

events.name: connector.schedule.skipped
events.description: A scheduled sync did not start, and why.

events.name: connector.run.failed
events.description: A sync run failed as a whole.

events.name: connector.page.failed
events.message: connector page failed; the run is partial
events.description: A connector failed to read one page, so its run is partial.

events.name: connector.page.unapplied
events.message: connector page could not be applied
events.description: A page a connector read could not be written to the graph.

events.name: connector.delivery.duplicate
events.description: A webhook delivery had already been applied by an earlier run, so nothing changed.

events.name: connector.webhook.failed
events.description: A verified webhook could not be applied.

events.name: sync.started
events.description: A connector began a run, scheduled, manual or from a webhook.

events.name: sync.page
events.description: A page a connector read was written to the graph. Pages count from 1.

events.name: sync.finished
events.description: A run ended, with how it ended, how long it took and what it wrote.

events.name: sync.runs.pruned
events.description: The retention job deleted the runs that finished before olderThan (#29, FR6). Logged even when it deleted none, so a quiet night still shows the job ran.

events.name: sync.runs.prune.failed
events.description: The retention job could not finish; the runs it had not reached are pruned the next night.

events.name: github.unreachable
events.description: The GitHub health check could not reach GitHub.

events.name: github.retrying
events.description: A GitHub request failed in a way worth retrying.

events.name: github.rate.limited
events.message: waiting for the GitHub rate limit to reset
events.description: GitHub's rate limit was reached; the connector waits for it rather than failing.

events.name: github.webhook.ignored
events.description: A GitHub webhook of a type the connector does not use.

events.name: github.webhook.malformed
events.message: verified GitHub webhook was not JSON
events.description: A GitHub webhook passed its signature check but its body could not be read.

events.name: github.dependencies.deferred
events.description: Dependencies on repositories not yet known were deferred to a later sync.

events.name: github.file.unreadable
events.description: A manifest or IaC file could not be read; the repository is still recorded.

events.name: github.file.skipped
events.description: A file was too large to read.

events.name: actions.deployment.unattributed
events.message: deployment not recorded; no artifact it deployed is known
events.description: A GitHub deployment was read whose run published no package version the connector could attribute to it, so there is no artifact to record it against.

events.name: actions.package.ambiguous
events.message: package version not attributed; more than one run could have published it
events.description: A package version was published while two or more runs of its repository were running, so it is credited to none of them rather than to a guess.

events.name: actions.webhook.ignored
events.description: A verified GitHub event the github-actions connector does not record, or one about an owner it was not configured to read.

events.name: servicenow.unreachable
events.description: The ServiceNow health check could not reach ServiceNow.

events.name: servicenow.health.refused
events.description: ServiceNow answered the health check with a refusal, usually of the credentials.

events.name: servicenow.retrying
events.description: A ServiceNow request failed in a way worth retrying.

events.name: servicenow.remote.invalid
events.message: CI names something that is not a git remote
events.description: A configuration item's repository field is not a git remote, so no link is written.

events.name: servicenow.link.unresolved
events.message: no repository for the CI's link
events.description: A configuration item names a repository the graph does not hold, so no link is written.
